title: Backwards-Compatible Migrations and Rollback Planning Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies backwards-compatible migrations and rollback planning?
options: Maintain overlapping readable contracts through adoption and rehearse recovery before irreversible contraction.
Assume rollback installs an older version
questions.answer: Maintain overlapping readable contracts through adoption and rehearse recovery before irreversible contraction.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A database migration tested from the immediately previous version covers every supported user upgrade path.
questions.explanation: Dropping or reinterpreting a field in the same release that introduces its replacement breaks old clients still active during staged rollout.

questions.prompt: Why is mobile rollback often a roll-forward hotfix?
questions.answer: Installed version codes and irreversible local/server changes can prevent simply downgrading users to an older binary.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
